title: Signal Distillation Playbook — customer threads & synthesis
summary: Working playbook for turning noisy customer threads into short, testable feature candidates and heuristics for prioritization. Emphasis on cost/latency tradeoffs and low-effort probes.
body:
Purpose:
- Provide an operational pattern for distilling multiple customer threads into prioritized, testable items.
- Make the heuristics explicit so eng/product can run fast micro-experiments.

Approach used:
- Collated 43 inbound threads (support, AE notes, enterprise calls) from Apr 1 — May 8 2029.
- Tagged each thread on three axes: user impact (low/med/high), frequency (1-off/occasional/common), blocker vs enhancement.
- Ran quick affinity clustering with 12 contributors (CS + Solutions).

Top emergent themes (raw):
1) Observability blind spots during fallbacks — customers see degraded model outputs but can’t tell why fallback triggered. Common ask: clearer reason codes + replay.
2) Cost surprises for bursty inference — teams hit unpredictable spikes when batch/caching config not tuned for chat workloads.
3) Private deployment onboarding friction — infra templates mismatch customer VPCs, docs outdated.
4) Output stability after quantization — a few enterprise customers report hallucination increase after moving to 4-bit profiles.
5) Fine-grained per-route throttles — customers want cost controls at route/feature level, not just project-level quotas.

Signal examples and one-line customer quotes:
- "We saw a fallback but don't know whether it was capacity, model mismatch, or policy." — FinTech integration lead
- "Monthly bill jumped 3x after a marketing spike — can't trace token hotspots." — Product manager at midmarket SaaS
- "Docs made it sound plug-and-play but our VPC peering blew up config wise." — On-prem platform engineer
- "Quantized model cut cost but replies became flaky on long contexts." — Research lead at enterprise

Heuristic prioritization matrix (explicit rules we used):
- Rule A: Any ask marked blocker + high frequency => immediate triage and patch candidate.
- Rule B: High cost impact + medium frequency => design micro-experiment to quantify unit-economics.
- Rule C: Low dev cost ideas with any customer anchor => ship as beta feature behind flag.

Microfeature proposals (short, actionable):
1) Fallback reason header + replay token (ship behind flag) — show: reason=capacity|policy|model-variant and include replay id for ops. Estimated effort: 2 sprint-days backend + 1 UI day. Risk: low. Cost impact: small (adds tracing metadata). Owner: eng-sre.
2) Route-level soft-budgets (alert + throttle) — per-route token thresholds that trigger alerts then soft-throttles. PoC: implement on routing layer with metrics hook. Estimated effort: 3 engineer-weeks. Potential savings: medium-high for customers with bursty traffic. Owner: product-hosted-api + infra.
3) Quantization regression suite (eval harness) — create focused evals for customers before they flip to low-bit profiles. Build a small dataset per-customer (10–20 prompts) and run nightly. Effort: 2 eng-weeks + small infra. Benefit: reduce regresion risk, speed adoption of quantization. Owner: applied-ml.
4) VPC onboarding checklist + terraform templates repo — short playbook and sample TF. Effort: 4 docs days + 1 eng-day to sanitize templates. Owner: private-deployments + solutions-engineering.

Quick cost/latency rough numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Fallback metadata: negligible token cost; storage for replays < $0.10/customer-month.
- Route soft-budgets: could avoid 20–40% of burst token spend for noisy workloads (customer-provided estimate).
- Quantization eval harness: infra cost small but could reduce regressions that otherwise cause large downstream debugging cost.

Proposed experiments (week-by-week plan):
- Week 0: Triage top 6 threads, assign owners, create JIRA tickets (JIRA-CS-9821 seeds).
- Week 1: Implement fallback-reason header in canary (select 4 customers). Measure signal clarity and CS reduction in follow-ups.
- Week 2–3: Prototype route soft-budget alerts in sandbox; pick two customers for alpha test.
- Week 3–4: Build quantization evaluation harness; run against one enterprise's seed prompts and report diffs.

Customer communication snippets (for CS/AE):
- "We’re rolling out clearer fallback reasons to help you quickly identify why a request degraded. Expect a small header and a replay link in logs."
- "We can run a short quantization checklist on your seed prompts to validate before switching profiles."

Open questions / unknowns we need to answer:
- What is the acceptable replay retention window for customers with strict privacy requirements? (CS to check with Legal)
- Can routing metrics be emitted at per-route granularity without a large telemetry cost? (infra spike required)
- Which customers have representative seed prompts for quant evals — who will own collection?

Decision forks and suggested defaults (for product discussions):
- Default soft-budget action: send alert -> 10% soft-throttle -> escalate to hard-throttle only after opt-in.
- Quantization rollout gating: require green on the customer's 10-seed prompt diff + automated BLEU/ROUGE style checks tailored to task.

Next steps (owners and due dates):
- Create JIRA EPIC and child tickets for the three microfeatures — Owner: Maya Chen — Due: 2029-05-20.
- Kickoff sync with applied-ml for quant eval harness — Owner: Ethan Rivera — Due: 2029-05-17.
- Draft customer-facing note for fallback reasons — Owner: Priya Kapoor — Due: 2029-05-18.

Notes to self / meeting fragments:
- CS asked for sample logs in the next partner call — bring replay demo.
- Consider tying fallback reason IDs to rollout policies so we can A/B different messaging.
- Quick win: add a note in onboarding docs about expected billing behavior for bursty chat flows.

Appendix: raw thread IDs used for clustering (samples)
- SLACK thread: #customer-xyz-2029-04-23 (support), ticket: SUP-4412, AE notes: AE-688, enterprise call summary 2029-04-30.
- Support ticket: SUP-4479 (billing spike), customer: ShopTribe.
- Enterprise: OnPrem rollout call notes 2029-04-29 (Jonas present).

If this doc looks good, I propose we convert into an EPIC with three child JIRA tickets (visibility: CS + Eng) and run the fallback reason canary for 2 weeks.

---
End of playbook draft.

(Internal: keep this living; update weekly with experiment outcomes and customer feedback snippets.)
